name: Prana
zone: Head / face (shared with Udana) and the chest (shared with Samana)
direction: Inward and downward — enters at the nose and mouth, moves down the throat and settles in the chest.
function: Intake: breathing in, receiving. The Praśna Upaniṣad places Prāṇa itself in the eye, ear, mouth and nose.
practice: On a slow inhalation, feel the breath enter at the nostrils and come to rest in the chest. Let the chest receive it without effort.

name: Samana
zone: The middle — around the navel, overlapping the chest zone
direction: Converging and balancing — currents arrive from the sides and from the chest, spiral into the navel, then radiate evenly.
function: Assimilation: 'leads the offered food to equality' — digestion and the even distribution of nourishment.
practice: At the turn of the breath, rest attention at the navel. Feel the in-breath and out-breath meet and balance there.

name: Apana
direction: Downward and outward — from the navel to the perineum and out through the base of the seat, like a cleansing wave.
function: Elimination and release. The Praśna Upaniṣad places Apāna in the organs of excretion and generation.
practice: On a long exhalation, let the breath settle downward through the pelvis into the ground. Release without pushing.

name: Udana
direction: Upward — rises from the chest through the throat into the head along the central channel, ending in a glow at the crown.
function: Ascent, speech and expression. In the Praśna Upaniṣad Udāna rises 'through one' channel and leads the departing self onward.
practice: At the end of an exhalation, feel a quiet upward lift through the throat toward the crown. Keep it light and brief.

name: Vyana
zone: The entire body (the large outer oval)
direction: Pervasive and radial — from the heart outward through the arms, legs and skin to the boundary of the body, then back in.
function: Circulation and coordination. The Praśna Upaniṣad says Vyāna moves in the hundred-and-one heart nadis and their branches.
practice: In the pause between breaths, feel the whole body at once, from the heart to the skin, as a single field.
